mechanism.domainTask: Open-ended optimization of programs, algorithms, and systems by jointly evolving candidate solutions and the search strategies that generate them
mechanism.populationDetail: The solution database \(D_t\) accumulates every evaluated candidate without an explicit island, tree, or partitioned population structure. The separate strategy database H stores historical search strategies and their contextual performance.
mechanism.archiveDetail: No separate bounded elite archive is specified; best-score queries are computed over the accumulated solution database.
mechanism.replacementDetail: New evaluated solutions are appended permanently to \(D_t\). A valid new strategy replaces the active strategy, but this is strategy-level replacement rather than candidate-population replacement.
mechanism.generationDetail: The active strategy chooses among local refinement, structural variation, and free-form variation of candidate solution(s). The paper also describes combining complementary parent/inspiration ideas in a case study, but does not consistently distinguish true parents from contextual inspirations.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Evaluator returns scalar score and auxiliary artifacts; search strategy uses score statistics, frontier/population descriptors, progress since improvement, and parent-selection frequency. The precise auxiliary artifacts passed to solution-generation prompts are task-dependent and not fully specified.
mechanism.parentSelection: strategy_dependent_selection_from_global_solution_database; can include greedy, stratified_multiobjective, random, or UCB policies; exact general arity unspecified
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: The formal context permits one or more candidate parents; inspirations are separate in notation but the case study sometimes describes blending their ideas. Outer-loop strategy-parent selection is score-biased over strategy history H, with inspirations informed by historical performance and population-state similarity.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: The outer loop evolves search strategies as first-class objects using a strategy-history population, state-conditioned strategy performance, and LLM mutation; this meta-evolution layer is not directly represented by the current candidate-focused taxonomy.

provenance.citationWarning: Survey currently cites EvoX in the introduction and application overview only. Proposed mechanism placements are not current citations. Multi-Parent Fusion is not assigned because true candidate ancestry versus inspiration is underspecified; per-run model setting is also unclear.
